origin: cwe/502/go Key Principles: gob will happily instantiate and populate any registered struct field - including privileged ones like IsAdmin or Balance - from untrusted input

finding.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
finding.summary: ProcessNextJob passes an untrusted message-queue payload straight to gob.NewDecoder().Decode() into a Job struct that carries the privileged IsAdmin field, so a crafted queue message can set IsAdmin true and have runJob execute the job with elevated privileges.

trap: Replacing gob.NewDecoder(r).Decode(&job) with json.NewDecoder(r).Decode(&job) into the same Job struct removes gob's arbitrary-type-instantiation risk but does not close this finding: encoding/json will still populate IsAdmin straight from the attacker-supplied message, because the struct being decoded into still carries a privileged field alongside the client-settable ones. The fix needs a purpose-built DTO containing only Command and Priority - the fields a queue message is allowed to set - with IsAdmin (and any other privileged field) resolved separately from a server-side source, never from the decoded payload, regardless of which format decodes it.
must_preserve: ProcessNextJob still decodes a queue message's Command and Priority and runs the job with those values. Whether a job runs with elevated privileges is decided by the server, independent of any field present in the queue message, so a message claiming an admin job is not allowed to run with elevated privileges.
